# Windows Game Explorer v2.5.0

> A complete owned-games catalogue in Game Explorer Studio, two new storefront libraries, a single Windows-installable gate, and one CLI dispatcher for every workflow.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Release Version** | `v2.5.0` |

| **Release Classification** | Packaged Application Release |
| **License** | [MIT](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) |
| **Release Channel** | Stable / Production |

---

## 📋 Overview

**Windows Game Explorer v2.5.0** finishes the owned-games catalogue that began in the unified Game Explorer Studio shell. The Game Catalogue is now a real, paged list of every game you own on a supported storefront — installed or not — with search, storefront/state/genre/tag/year/rating/playtime/family filters, six sort keys, and page sizes from 12 to 96 rows. It is intentionally a single list view: no details pane, no launching, and no install-folder management. Installing is handed to the storefront's own client through its official protocol, while playing stays in the File Explorer **Games** view.

This release also broadens where owned games come from. Ubisoft Connect ownership is read from the client's read-only caches (59 verified titles on the development machine), and Epic ownership can come from an optional, read-only **legendary** cache (250 verified titles). A centralized Windows-installable gate removes console, mobile, macOS and Linux-only editions across every source, and edition-aware title normalization keeps the same game owned in different editions collapsed into one row. Finally, the four root batch launchers are replaced by one `game-explorer.bat` dispatcher with a PSScriptAnalyzer zero-diagnostic gate.

---

## ✨ Highlights

- **Owned-Games Catalogue** — Paged, filterable and sortable list of every owned storefront game, with delegated installs and store-page actions.
- **Ubisoft Connect & Epic Owned Libraries** — Read-only Ubisoft ownership cache plus an optional authenticated legendary cache for Epic, verified at 59 and 250 owned titles respectively.
- **Windows-Installable Gate** — One centralized filter drops console/mobile/macOS/Linux-only editions across Steam, Epic, GOG, itch, Xbox and Ubisoft.
- **Edition-Aware Deduplication** — Edition suffixes stay in the source label while the canonical title merges cross-store duplicates into one row.
- **Single CLI Dispatcher** — `game-explorer.bat` owns build, test, lint, package, release, registration, signing and artwork commands without opening a second window.

## 🔍 What's Changed

### 🆕 Added
- **Game Catalogue completion** — real paged list with sticky column header, `ThemeScroll` gutter, empty state, status line, and page sizes 12/24/48/96.
- **Catalogue filtering and sorting** — search plus storefront, install state, genre, tag, year, rating, playtime and family-sharing filters; title, release date, playtime, last played, storefront and install size sorts in either direction; Reset filters.
- **Ubisoft Connect owned library** — read-only `cache\ownership` and `cache\configuration\configurations` parsing (length-delimited protobuf), localized titles, official CDN box art, and `uplay://launch/<installId>/0` install delegation.
- **Epic owned library through legendary (optional)** — read-only `assets.json` plus per-app metadata, Windows/Win32 preference, `ue` namespace skip, and `com.epicgames.com` launcher installation.
- **Windows-only catalogue gate** — `StorefrontSource::windowsInstallable` plus `FilterWindowsInstallableOwnedGames()` using Xbox `availablePlatforms`, GOG `osCompatibility`, itch `scanned_platforms` and batched Steam `IStoreBrowseService` evidence.
- **Catalogue editions** — `StorefrontSource::editionLabel` and `ExtractBaseTitle()` keep edition suffixes out of canonical titles while install/store-page pickers name the edition.
- **Unified CLI dispatcher** — `game-explorer.bat` with `build`, `test`, `lint`, `package`, `release`, `register`, `unregister`, `sign`, `art`, `setup-signing` and `help`.
- **PSScriptAnalyzer gate** — `scripts/lint.ps1`, enforced by `release` and CI.
- **Tests** — 61 unit tests, including 21 catalogue cases, the Ubisoft cache and legendary mapping.

### 🔄 Changed
- **Installs are delegated only** — the catalogue hands the request to the storefront client and reports the result; install location always belongs to the client.
- **Installed sources are explicit** — an already-installed edition is labelled `(Installed)` and selecting it directs the user to the File Explorer Games view instead of reinstalling.
- **Registration is fail-fast** — `register.ps1` / `unregister.ps1` verify elevation and print the exact rerun command instead of self-elevating.
- **Portable package layout** — the ZIP ships `game-explorer.bat` plus `scripts\register.ps1`, `unregister.ps1` and `_common.ps1`; the NSIS installer ships and retires the same layout.
- **Catalogue is list-only** — no per-title details pane by design; rows and toolbar/footer actions are the whole interaction surface.

### 🐛 Fixed
- **Installer license wrapping** — the NSIS license page reads `installer/LICENSE.txt`, whose paragraphs stay on one line so rich-edit wrapping fits the dialog instead of stacking on top of 78-column hard breaks.
- **Themed checkbox/radio state** — `ThemeControls` stores `BM_SETCHECK` and answers `BM_GETCHECK`, so owner-drawn checkboxes and radios keep their state.
- **Catalogue field repaint** — removed the dead install-base rectangle and aligned the footer band layout with the delegated-install model.

### 🗑️ Removed & Deprecated
- **Root batch launchers** — `build.bat`, `release.bat`, `register.bat` and `unregister.bat` were replaced by `game-explorer.bat`.
- **Tag-triggered release workflow** — `.github/workflows/release.yml` was retired because it never produced the shipped release set; manual `game-explorer.bat release` packaging is authoritative.
- **Install base folder and `InstallTargets`** — a storefront install URI cannot target a folder, so the pre-created base-folder scaffolding was removed.
- **Per-title catalogue detail pane** — explicitly rejected; the catalogue stays a single list view.
- **Planned relocation and install-progress tracking** — dropped by user decision (2026-10-26) together with install-location handling; M18 is Windows 10 vs 11 shell compatibility research.

### 🔐 Security, Hygiene & Compliance
- **Read-only storefront access** — every catalogue source is read-only; the app never writes to storefront manifests, caches or databases.
- **Secret masking** — Steam Web API keys and RetroAchievements keys remain masked with `ES_PASSWORD` in the Studio.
- **No third-party scrapers** — catalogue rows come from official storefront APIs and local caches only.
- **MIT licensing** — canonical MIT text is installed and the installer-only copy is used solely for the license page.
